We implemented a house rule last night about death saves and I thought I'd share (even though it's nothing special).

When you roll a 1 on a death save, RAW, you get two failures. When you roll a 20, however, you automatically come back to life with 1hp. We decided that's not balanced with itself, so from now on in our games, rolling a 1 on a death save means you're automatically dead.

This will make lower levels more deadly for sure. Once characters hit fifth level and have Revivify available it becomes less serious, and of course once they hit 9th and have access to Raise Dead it just makes for a good tavern story.

I like it save for one caveat. I don't like giving players a challenge without giving them a tool to address that challenge. Throwing a monster that can only take damage from magical sources, for example, prior to the party receiving magical weapons/class features, makes for a poor setup. So in your example, I would personally only apply this houserule at level 5 and on.
